newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil, fuel oil sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil, fuel oil sharply lower.

text.p: Singapore oil product prices extended losses on Thursday, with gas oil and fuel oil dropping sharply, traders said.
They said the market remained bearish despite large draws in Singapore middle distillate and residue stocks as regional demand remained muted.

Singapore mid-distillates stocks fell 1.8 million barrels to 6.5 million barrels for the week ended Jan 15, while residue stocks fell 926,000 barrels to 10.1 million barrels. Despite this, as much as one million barrels of gas oil were offered and Singapore refiners were said to be forced to store their oil in independent storage terminal. Physical and swaps gas oil fell under $28 with the paper market going into contango due to the nearby supply glut. The lowest offer of physical gas oil was seen at $27.70 for early February lifting fob, compared with Wednesday's $28.75.

Light distillate stocks rose a marginal 75,000 barrels to 5.9 million barrels. Gasoline was assessed long with supplies heard available from China and Singapore, while regional demand was limited to India. Levels firmed with a bid for 92-octane raised to $25.90 a barrel, up 60 cents from Wednesday.

Naphtha fundamentals were supported by steady demand and tight supplies. In the Mideast, traders said limited supplies made naphtha the strongest product, pushing premiums to $13 a tonne over spot quotes. A major in Singapore offered two cargoes lifting early/late February at nearly $1 a barrel over spot quotes, fob.
